long_description:
Seat at the Table documents the rise of South Asian Americans in U.S. politics, tracing their journey from the margins towards power.

About this Event

Seat at the Table follows several prominent South Asian political candidates during the 2024 election cycle, alongside a community galvanized by the groundbreaking campaign of the first South Asian presidential candidate. Within a hundred years, South Asians in America have gone from being disenfranchised, to seeing the first South Asian presidential candidate on a major party’s ticket.
Join us to see thsi film and hear from the filmmakers and others on rise of South Asians in this arena. 
When: Thursday, Nov 19th at 6 PM
Where: City College of NY, Shepard Hall, Room 291 (second floor)
259 Convent Avenue at 140th Street (SE Corner) ID needed to enter the building.
To get there: #1 to 137th street, ABCD to 145th Street. Accessible mode: #6 to 125th Street, M101 to 140th street. 
Building and theater is accessible. CART available. Light Refreshments.
Presented by Third World Newsrteel, the Documentary Forum at CCNY and AAARI (Asian American/Asian Research Institute at CUNY)

With unprecedented access to congressional and state-level campaigns, as well as grassroots organizing efforts, the film captures a historic year for the South Asian diaspora as more candidates than ever run for office, providing us a rare front-row seat to an immigrant community awakening to its power in America.

Director/ Producer
SARITA KHURANA is an award-winning filmmaker whose work includes A SUITABLE GIRL (2017 Best New Documentary Director at Tribeca Film Festival, Netflix, Amazon); THE LAST RESORT (2025, Best Documentary at ISAFF Canada); and CROSSROADS (2022, Emmy Nominee as part of the series ASIAN AMERICAN STORIES OF RESILIENCE AND BEYOND; Winner Best Documentary, Chicago SAFF).
